<!-- pr-reviewer: 5f22d9d5e176c566633785faff09c5fb9ff10b29 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Reviewed at head `5f22d9d5`, trial-merged locally with `upstream/main` `1f6a74be` (the merge has no conflicts; nothing was pushed). Safety tier: this PR changes Tormach posted motion.

### What looks good
- `xyFirst` writes `G0 Z<clearance>` before the first X/Y traverse of an upright section. The clearance is `ClearancePlane`, else `RetractPlane`, and never below the move's own Z (`assets/posts/tormach.cps` `traverseZ`).
- A refused first traverse writes no motion. All six callers (rapid, feed, arc, probe guard, probe move, canned cycle) return when `xyFirst` or `startXY` returns false. This agrees with the rule from the #1636 review.
- Indexed (A not 0) sections keep the order of #785. A section that turns back to `A0` gets the clearance Z after `G0 A0`.
- `startXY` does not write a second `G0 Z` when the traverse height is already the feed's start height.
- The order at a tool change agrees with #1606 (see the table below).
- Real jobs always state the plane: `post::dump` writes `PARAM ClearancePlane` and `PARAM RetractPlane` for each section (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs:260-261`), and `posting.rs` fills them from the operation heights (`clearance_z: hs.clearance`, `retract_z: hs.retract.unwrap_or(hs.clearance)`). Thus the refusal fires only on a hand-written or legacy stream that states no plane.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/1614-toolchange-clearance.md` records the choices and what is taken on trust. The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #1614`. No `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot PNG, process file, `build.rs`, `.github/` or dependency change. `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is not a process file, so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is necessary.

### Golden diff (scripted, against `upstream/main` `1f6a74be`)
- 32 `.nc` files changed. All are Tormach mill programs. Each file has exactly one inserted line, and the line is `G0 Z<value>`. There are no deleted or changed lines.
- In each file, the next line is the bare `G0 X.. Y..` traverse. At a tool change, the `G0 Z` comes after the `G53 G0 Z0` lift of #1606 and after `S.. M3` / `M8` (or `M5` for a probe).
- Coverage over all 33 Tormach mill goldens at the merged head: 34 program starts and tool changes have an X/Y traverse after them. All 34 have the `G0 Z` line immediately before the traverse. 0 are missing. The two indexed sections at `A-90` and `A90` in `microarc_test_part.nc` keep their own order, as intended.
- The 4 contour goldens that took main's side (`contour_disc_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, inch `contour_plate_with_hole`) differ from main only by the one inserted line. Thus they carry main's #1577 climb change plus the insert, and nothing more.

### Order at a tool change (`drill_peck.nc`)

| # | Line | From |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `G53 G0 Z0` | retract before the change |
| 2 | `G30` | PathPilot tool-change position |
| 3 | `T4 M6` | tool change |
| 4 | `G43 H4` | length offset |
| 5 | `G53 G0 Z0` | #1596 / PR #1606 lift |
| 6 | `S1500 M3` | spindle |
| 7 | `M8` | coolant |
| 8 | `G0 Z0.2362` | **this PR** |
| 9 | `G0 X0.7874 Y0.3937` | first X/Y traverse |

Is line 8 redundant after line 5? No. Line 5 goes to the top of machine travel. Line 8 goes to a stated work height. A work Z cannot be above the top of travel, so line 8 is always a move down or no move. If the clearance is above the top of travel, the control refuses line 8 at its Z limit and stops. That is the #1614 case, and that is the intended result.

Can line 8 go down at the tool-change X/Y? Yes, it always goes down in place, at the `G30` X/Y (Tormach's `M6` does not move X/Y). This is not the Carvera problem from #1632: on the Carvera the firmware parks the spindle near the tool rack, and the post does not know where. On the Tormach, the `G30` position is the operator's own preset. The descent stops at the clearance plane, which is above the stock. The decision file records that the post trusts nothing under the `G30` X/Y to be taller than the clearance plane. I agree with that trust. It is safer than the bare traverse below the part top.

### State block merge (`tormach.cps`)
- Lines in `upstream/main` (and in `389fe96c`) that are not in the merged head: only the lines that this PR replaces on purpose (the old `xyFirst` / `startXY` bodies, the old caller lines and the old `onSectionEnd`).
- Lines in `b510bac5` that are not in the merged head: only the caller lines that `5f22d9d5` changes to return on a refusal.
- `clearZ`, `afterAsk`, `setupNext`, `onParameter` (`AfterOperation`, `SetupChange`) and `afterOp()` from #1532 are all present. No line from either side is lost.

### Mutation checks (each applied to `tormach.cps`, tests run, file restored)

| Mutation | Result | Failing tests (examples) |
|---|---|---|
| Remove the `G0 Z` lift | caught | 3 of 4 `tormach_traverse_clearance`, 6 `recorded_streams`, `golden_cl`, `tormach_post::the_first_move_after_a_tool_change_positions_xy_with_z_up` |
| Write the `G0 Z` after the X/Y | caught | same set as above |
| Use the move's own Z, not the clearance | caught | 5 `recorded_streams`, `golden_cl` (`every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact`), `program_units`, `tormach_post` |
| Remove the max with the move's own Z | caught | `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height` |
| Remove the `RetractPlane` fallback | caught | `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated` |
| No `G0 Z` after the second and later tool changes | caught | `tormach_post::the_first_move_after_a_tool_change_positions_xy_with_z_up` |
| Remove the refusal `return false` in `xyFirst` | caught | `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` |
| Remove the caller return in `onRapid` | caught | `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` |

### Local results (merged with main, macOS, debug)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all 51 test binaries and lib) | all pass; `tormach_traverse_clearance` 4/4, `recorded_streams` 12/12, `script_tormach` 11/11, `probe_tormach` 7/7, `work_offset_index` 9/9, `first_traverse_clearance` 7/7, `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family` 9/9 |
| `camcraft-app` targeted | `golden_cl` 33/33, `recorded_post_streams` 5/5, `conformance` 7/7, `program_units` 7/7, `microarc_test_part` 2/2, `post_cycle_feed_spindle` 8/8, `tormach_post` 10/10, `tormach_toolchange_lift` 3/3, `tormach_fourth_axis` 12/12, `tormach_safe_retract` 4/4, `tormach_program_end` 3/3, `tormach_routers` 5/5, `tormach_end_units` 7/7, `tormach_machines` 6/6, `tormach_lathes` 2/2, `posting` 17/17, `after_op` 10/10, `probe_op` 12/12, others pass |
| `camcraft-app` all test binaries (`--tests`, 425 binaries, 22 min) | 3057 pass, 2 fail, 23 ignored. The 2 failures are `lead_approach::the_reported_keep_down_helix_pocket_enters_every_level_once` and `lead_approach::the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`. That is the known red on main (#1675, fixed by PR #1676). This PR does not change toolpath generation, so I do not count them against it. |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. The refusal message is once for each program (`traverseRefused`). If the first section is refused, a later section with no plane is also not written, but it gets no message of its own. Because the program is refused already, I think this is correct. I note it only so that it is a known choice.
2. A section that keeps its tool does not reset `xyUnknown`, so it gets no new clearance Z. That is the same as on main and is not in the scope of this PR (see #1626).
3. The PR still has the stale `conflicts` label from before the merge of main. GitHub now reports MERGEABLE. I change the label below.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Post-merge record. The PR merged at 17:02Z before this review finished. I found no blocker in the diff.**

## What looks good
- `assets/posts/tormach.cps`: `xyFirst` writes `G0 Z<clearance>` before the first X/Y traverse of an upright section. The clearance is `ClearancePlane`, else `RetractPlane`, and never below the move's own Z. The Z uses the same work-offset helper as the other moves.
- Refusal: a stream with neither plane gets one named message. `xyFirst` and `startXY` return false. All six callers (rapid, feed, arc, probe guard, probe move, canned cycle) return before they write. X/Y stays unknown, so no later move is written and no second message appears. A refused first traverse writes no move. This matches the rule from the review of #1636.
- Indexed (4th-axis) sections keep their own order. The traverse Z logic is skipped for them.
- `startXY` does not write a second `G0 Z` when the traverse already was at the start Z. Good.
- Goldens: I checked all `.nc` files with `git diff -U0 origin/main...`. Each of the 32 files has exactly one added line and no deleted line. Each added line is a `G0 Z<value>`. No other difference by file.
- Merge commit 232133a1: the remerge-diff shows only the 4 contour goldens (regenerated on main's side, 15 lines each) and the 3-line state block in `tormach.cps`. Both sides of the state block are kept (`clearZ`, `afterAsk`, `setupNext`). The result is as the PR body says.
- `legacy_program.rs` has no remerge change. No snapshot PNG changed. `Process change: yes` applies (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is a post note, not a process file).

## Results
- Runner run 43617268075 for this head: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43617268075. It was still in progress (quick gate and clippy) when the PR merged and when I wrote this. I give no pass for it. I did not run local builds.
- The PR body states: post suites pass; two `lead_approach` tests fail on main without this PR (known, #1675).

## What was not exercised on a real control
- The PathPilot Hub run used `drill_peck` before the merge of main, in the Hub simulator (770MX sim v2.14.4). It showed that the low traverse is gone and every move stayed above the part.
- Not run on a real machine. Not run for the head with the refusal change. Not run for probing, indexed or canned-cycle programs other than `drill_peck`. The "setup that cannot clear stops at the Z limit" case is taken on trust from the control (the decision file says so).

## Notes (not blocking)
- Opening dip: the Hub run still showed a G30 dip, which is #1626 and is separate.
- Please check the run above for the final result.

A maintainer has merged this PR.
